title: Dispatch: finding registry v1 corrections (attempt 2)
description:
SUPERVISOR REVIEW OF ATTEMPT 1 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6.1, commit b32bdfc).
Attempt 1 landed a real registry with complete ALIAS coverage — 70 aliases
across opus (36), sol (14), fable (8), indep (12), all resolving. Keep that.
Four defects must be fixed before this bead can close.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== DEFECT 1: OVER-CLUSTERING DESTROYS CLOSURE EVIDENCE ===
15 canonical rows absorb 70 aliases. Several rows bundle MULTIPLE FINDINGS FROM
THE SAME REVIEW, which is prima facie evidence that distinct defects were merged:

  source-authority          fable:F1 + fable:F5 + fable:F7  (three different
                            Fable findings: unsupported Starting Wealth table;
                            synthesized table headers; synthesized choice
                            sourceText labels — these are not one defect)
  creature-procedures       opus:F-25,F-26,F-28,F-29,F-31,F-32 (six)
  segmentation-and-locators indep:008,009,010,012 + opus:F-15,F-17,F-30 (seven)
  taxonomy-and-structured   opus:F-10,F-13,F-14,F-16,F-34 (five)

Why this matters: the registry exists so that at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4 every
finding can be proven individually non-repeating. If closing "source-authority"
is the only available evidence, a repair can close the row while the
starting-wealth fabrication is still present. Coarse rows make the zero-repeat
certification unfalsifiable.

RULE: two aliases from the SAME review may share a row only when they genuinely
name the same defect, and the row must then carry a `clusterJustification`
field explaining why that review listed it twice. Otherwise split into separate
rows. Cross-review aliases naming one defect are exactly what a canonical row is
for — keep collapsing those.

Read the per-review finding tables in
/mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md (sections "Independent Sol
audit", "Opus 5 original audit", "Opus 5 amended creature/magic-item audit",
"GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit", "Fable 5 audit") and split against what each finding
actually says, not against its theme.

=== DEFECT 2: MISSING statusReasoning FIELD ===
The spec required `statusReasoning`, required whenever status is not
"accepted". The committed rows have no such field. Add it, populate it for every
non-accepted row, and add a test that a non-accepted row without reasoning fails
validation.

=== DEFECT 3: THE LANGUAGE FINDING IS MISPLACED AND MIS-STATUSED ===
indep:011 is "falsely closed language universe" and the plan routes it to C1/C3
(= eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1 and .19.3.3). Attempt 1 buried it inside the
`source-authority` row owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1. That is the wrong defect
and the wrong owner.

The parent bead requires this finding to be represented as an ADJUDICATION /
POLICY question, NOT as a projection defect — an open language-choice universe
is a campaign-ruling extension point, not a compiler bug. Give it its own row,
the correct owning bead, and a non-"accepted" status (`ambiguous` is the
closest fit in the allowed set) with statusReasoning saying explicitly that it
is a policy/adjudication decision routed to campaign rulings.

=== DEFECT 4: SEVEN QUERIES FOR FIFTEEN ROWS ===
Rows share coarse membership queries (recordsWithSourceAuthorityRisk,
recordsWithLocatorOrOwnershipEvidence, recordsWithExecutionReadiness, ...). A
query that cannot discriminate one row's membership from another's is not
membership evidence — it is a category label with a count attached.

Every row needs its OWN query that enumerates that row's exact membership. After
the DEFECT 1 split there will be more rows, so expect roughly one query per row.
Where two rows genuinely share a membership set, they were probably the same
defect — reconsider the split rather than sharing the query.

Add a test asserting that no two rows share a membershipQuery name unless the
row carries an explicit `sharedQueryJustification`.

=== ALSO CHECK ===
sol:CAP-009 is currently in the `spell-procedures` row, but
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3's "Closes findings" line claims it for bidirectional
provenance. Resolve the ownership against the plan text and record which reading
you took.

=== UNCHANGED CONSTRAINTS FROM ATTEMPT 1 ===
No hand-copied totals (391, 399, 77, 79, 794, 1016, 1813) anywhere. Fully
qualified aliases only — never a bare "F1" or "CAP-002"; engine:F*, fable:F*,
opus:F-*, sol:CAP-*, indep:* are the five prefixes. sol:CAP-002 stays NARROWED
with the no-regression requirement on existing typed condition effects. Records
use the `key` field, not `id`; executionReadiness lives at
`record.data.executionReadiness`.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
This worktree already contains attempt 1's committed work; you are extending it,
not starting over. Run `npm ci` FIRST (worktrees have no node_modules of their
own). Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under FILES YOU OWN. A sibling dispatch is running
  in parallel on a disjoint file set. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge. Committed work on
  your branch is a complete handoff.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete any existing test. Do NOT regenerate the pack.
* Do not "fix" attempt 1 by deleting its work; the defects below are gaps in
  coverage and fidelity, not wrong direction.
acceptance_criteria:
• No row bundles two aliases from the same review without a clusterJustification.
• statusReasoning exists and is populated for every non-accepted row, enforced by a test.
• The language finding has its own row, correct owning bead, non-accepted status, and adjudication/policy reasoning.
• Every row has a discriminating membership query; shared queries require explicit justification, enforced by a test.
• All 70 aliases still resolve to exactly one canonical row each.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
